title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 55
text:
10.5 The caution which must be given on:
(a) arrest; or
(b) all other occasions before a person is charged or informed they
may be prosecuted, see section 16, should, unless the restriction
on drawing adverse inferences from silence applies, see Annex C,
be in the following terms:
“You do not have to say anything, but I must caution you that if
you do not mention when questioned something which you later
rely on in Court, it may harm your defence. If you do say anything
it may be given in evidence.”
See Note 10G.

10.6 Annex C, paragraph 2 sets out the alternative terms of the caution
to be used when the restriction on drawing adverse inferences
from silence applies.

10.7 Minor deviations from the words of any caution given in
accordance with this Code do not constitute a breach of this Code,
provided the sense of the relevant caution is preserved. See Note
10D.
